verses.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα χωρισθεὶς ἐκ τῶν Ἀθηνῶν ἦλθεν εἰς Κόρινθον
verses.transliteration: Meta tauta chōristheis ek tōn Athēnōn ēlthen eis Korinthon
verses.literal: After this Paul left . . . Athens and went to Corinth
verses.literalPt: Depois disso, Paulo partiu de Atenas e foi a Corinto.

verses.original: καὶ εὑρών τινα Ἰουδαῖον ὀνόματι Ἀκύλαν Ποντικὸν τῷ γένει προσφάτως ἐληλυθότα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰταλίας καὶ Πρίσκιλλαν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ διὰ τὸ διατεταχέναι Κλαύδιον χωρίζεσθαι πάντας τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ἀπὸ τῆς Ῥώμης προσῆλθεν αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: kai heurōn tina Ioudaion onomati Akylan Pontikon tō genei prosphatōs elēlythota apo tēs Italias kai Priskillan gynaika autou dia to diatetachenai Klaudion chōrizesthai pantas tous Ioudaious apo tēs Rhōmēs prosēlthen autois
verses.literal: There he found a Jew named Aquila a native of Pontus who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave . . . Rome Paul went to visit them
verses.literalPt: Achando um judeu por nome Áquila, natural do Ponto, recém-chegado da Itália, e Priscila, sua mulher (por ter Cláudio decretado que todos os judeus saíssem de Roma), foi ter com eles

verses.original: καὶ διὰ τὸ ὁμότεχνον εἶναι ἔμενεν παρ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἠργάζετο ἦσαν γὰρ σκηνοποιοὶ τῇ τέχνῃ
verses.transliteration: kai dia to homotechnon einai emenen par’ autois kai ērgazeto ēsan gar skēnopoioi tē technē
verses.literal: and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade just as he was
verses.literalPt: e, por ser do mesmo ofício, com eles morava, e ali trabalhavam; pois o ofício deles era fabricar tendas.

verses.original: Διελέγετο δὲ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἔπειθέν τε Ἰουδαίους καὶ Ἕλληνας
verses.transliteration: Dielegeto de en tē synagōgē kata pan sabbaton epeithen te Ioudaious kai Hellēnas
verses.literal: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike
verses.literalPt: Todos os sábados discutia ele na sinagoga e persuadia a judeus e a gregos.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ κατῆλθον ἀπὸ τῆς Μακεδονίας ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος συνείχετο τῷ λόγῳ ὁ Παῦλος διαμαρτυρόμενος τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις εἶναι τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν
verses.transliteration: Hōs de katēlthon apo tēs Makedonias ho te Silas kai ho Timotheos syneicheto tō logō ho Paulos diamartyromenos tois Ioudaiois einai ton Christon Iēsoun
verses.literal: And when - Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia Paul devoted himself fully to the word testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ
verses.literalPt: Quando Silas e Timóteo desceram da Macedônia, Paulo estava ativamente ocupado com a palavra, testificando aos judeus que Jesus era o Cristo.

verses.original: ἀντιτασσομένων δὲ αὐτῶν καὶ βλασφημούντων ἐκτιναξάμενος τὰ ἱμάτια εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τὸ αἷμα ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν ὑμῶν καθαρὸς ἐγώ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πορεύσομαι
verses.transliteration: antitassomenōn de autōn kai blasphēmountōn ektinaxamenos ta himatia eipen pros autous To haima hymōn epi tēn kephalēn hymōn katharos egō apo tou nyn eis ta ethnē poreusomai
verses.literal: But when they opposed and insulted him he shook out his garments and told . . . them Your blood be on your own heads I am innocent of it From now on I will go to the Gentiles
verses.literalPt: Mas, como eles se opusessem e blasfemassem, sacudindo ele as vestes, disse-lhes: O vosso sangue venha sobre a vossa cabeça; eu estou limpo e desde agora vou para os gentios.

verses.original: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν εἰσῆλθεν εἰς οἰκίαν τινὸς ὀνόματι Τίτου Ἰούστου σεβομένου τὸν Θεόν οὗ ἡ οἰκία ἦν συνομοροῦσα τῇ συναγωγῇ
verses.transliteration: Kai metabas ekeithen eisēlthen eis oikian tinos onomati Titou Ioustou sebomenou ton Theon hou hē oikia ēn synomorousa tē synagōgē
verses.literal: So Paul left . . . the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus - a worshiper of God
verses.literalPt: Saindo dali, entrou em casa de um homem chamado Tício Justo, que era temente a Deus, e cuja casa era contígua à sinagoga.

verses.original: Κρίσπος δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος ἐπίστευσεν τῷ Κυρίῳ σὺν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν Κορινθίων ἀκούοντες ἐπίστευον καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο
verses.transliteration: Krispos de ho archisynagōgos episteusen tō Kyriō syn holō tō oikō autou kai polloi tōn Korinthiōn akouontes episteuon kai ebaptizonto
verses.literal: Crispus the synagogue leader and his whole household believed in the Lord And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized
verses.literalPt: Crispo, chefe da sinagoga, creu no Senhor, com toda a sua casa; e muitos coríntios, ouvindo, criam e eram batizados.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος ἐν νυκτὶ δι’ ὁράματος τῷ Παύλῳ Μὴ φοβοῦ ἀλλὰ λάλει καὶ μὴ σιωπήσῃς
verses.transliteration: Eipen de ho Kyrios en nykti di’ horamatos tō Paulō Mē phobou alla lalei kai mē siōpēsēs
verses.literal: One . . . night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision Do not be afraid keep on speaking do not be silent
verses.literalPt: De noite, disse o Senhor a Paulo, em uma visão: Não temas, mas fala e não te cales;

verses.original: διότι ἐγώ εἰμι μετὰ σοῦ καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιθήσεταί σοι τοῦ κακῶσαί σε διότι λαός ἐστί μοι πολὺς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ
verses.transliteration: dioti egō eimi meta sou kai oudeis epithēsetai soi tou kakōsai se dioti laos esti moi polys en tē polei tautē
verses.literal: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on . . . . . . . . . you because I have . . . many people in this city
verses.literalPt: porque eu sou contigo, e ninguém te porá a mão para te fazer mal, pois tenho muito povo nesta cidade.

verses.original: Ἐκάθισεν δὲ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ μῆνας ἓξ διδάσκων ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: Ekathisen de eniauton kai mēnas hex didaskōn en autois ton logon tou Theou
verses.literal: So Paul stayed for a year and a half . . . teaching the word of God among the Corinthians
verses.literalPt: Ali ficou um ano e seis meses, ensinando entre eles a palavra de Deus.

verses.original: Γαλλίωνος δὲ ἀνθυπάτου ὄντος τῆς Ἀχαΐας κατεπέστησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα
verses.transliteration: Galliōnos de anthypatou ontos tēs Achaias katepestēsan homothymadon hoi Ioudaioi tō Paulō kai ēgagon auton epi to bēma
verses.literal: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat
verses.literalPt: Sendo Gálio procônsul da Acaia, levantaram-se os judeus de comum acordo contra Paulo e, levando-o ao tribunal,

verses.original: λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ τὸν νόμον ἀναπείθει οὗτος τοὺς ἀνθρώπους σέβεσθαι τὸν Θεόν
verses.transliteration: legontes hoti Para ton nomon anapeithei houtos tous anthrōpous sebesthai ton Theon
verses.literal: This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law they said
verses.literalPt: disseram: Este persuade os homens a adorar a Deus de um modo contrário à Lei.

verses.original: Μέλλοντος δὲ τοῦ Παύλου ἀνοίγειν τὸ στόμα εἶπεν ὁ Γαλλίων πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους Εἰ μὲν ἦν ἀδίκημά τι ἢ ῥᾳδιούργημα πονηρόν ὦ Ἰουδαῖοι κατὰ λόγον ἂν ἀνεσχόμην ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: Mellontos de tou Paulou anoigein to stoma eipen ho Galliōn pros tous Ioudaious Ei men ēn adikēma ti ē rhadiourgēma ponēron ō Ioudaioi kata logon an aneschomēn hymōn
verses.literal: But just as Paul was about to speak . . . . . . Gallio told . . . the Jews If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime O Jews it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint
verses.literalPt: Estando Paulo para falar, disse Gálio aos judeus: Se fosse, com efeito, alguma injustiça ou crime perverso, ó judeus, de razão seria atender-vos;

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ζητήματά ἐστιν περὶ λόγου καὶ ὀνομάτων καὶ νόμου τοῦ καθ’ ὑμᾶς ὄψεσθε αὐτοί κριτὴς ἐγὼ τούτων οὐ βούλομαι εἶναι
verses.transliteration: ei de zētēmata estin peri logou kai onomatōn kai nomou tou kath’ hymas opsesthe autoi kritēs egō toutōn ou boulomai einai
verses.literal: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law settle it yourselves I refuse . . . to be a judge of such things
verses.literalPt: mas, se são questões de palavras, de nomes e da vossa Lei, cuidai vós lá disso; eu não quero ser juiz dessas coisas.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπήλασεν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ βήματος
verses.transliteration: kai apēlasen autous apo tou bēmatos
verses.literal: And he drove them away from the judgment seat
verses.literalPt: E fê-los sair do tribunal.

verses.original: Ἐπιλαβόμενοι δὲ πάντες Σωσθένην τὸν ἀρχισυνάγωγον ἔτυπτον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος καὶ οὐδὲν τούτων τῷ Γαλλίωνι ἔμελεν
verses.transliteration: Epilabomenoi de pantes Sōsthenēn ton archisynagōgon etypton emprosthen tou bēmatos kai ouden toutōn tō Galliōni emelen
verses.literal: At this the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat But none of this was of concern to Gallio
verses.literalPt: Todos pegaram em Sóstenes, chefe da sinagoga, e o espancavam diante do tribunal; e Gálio não se importava com nenhuma dessas coisas.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔτι προσμείνας ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἀποταξάμενος ἐξέπλει εἰς τὴν Συρίαν καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας κειράμενος ἐν Κενχρεαῖς τὴν κεφαλήν εἶχεν γὰρ εὐχήν
verses.transliteration: Ho de Paulos eti prosmeinas hēmeras hikanas tois adelphois apotaxamenos exeplei eis tēn Syrian kai syn autō Priskilla kai Akylas keiramenos en Kenchreais tēn kephalēn eichen gar euchēn
verses.literal: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made and then he sailed for Syria accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila
verses.literalPt: Paulo, tendo ficado ali ainda muitos dias, despediu-se dos irmãos e navegou com Priscila e Áquila para a Síria, depois de haver mandado rapar a cabeça em Cencreia, pois tinha voto.

verses.original: Κατήντησαν δὲ εἰς Ἔφεσον κἀκείνους κατέλιπεν αὐτοῦ αὐτὸς δὲ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν διελέξατο τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις
verses.transliteration: Katēntēsan de eis Epheson kakeinous katelipen autou autos de eiselthōn eis tēn synagōgēn dielexato tois Ioudaiois
verses.literal: When they reached . . . Ephesus Paul left . . . Priscilla and Aquila He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews
verses.literalPt: Chegados a Éfeso, deixou-os ali; mas ele, entrando na sinagoga, discutiu com os judeus.

verses.original: ἐρωτώντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ πλείονα χρόνον μεῖναι οὐκ ἐπένευσεν
verses.transliteration: erōtōntōn de autōn epi pleiona chronon meinai ouk epeneusen
verses.literal: When they asked him to stay for a while longer . . . he declined
verses.literalPt: Rogando-lhe estes que ficasse mais tempo, não anuiu,

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἀποταξάμενος καὶ εἰπών Πάλιν ἀνακάμψω πρὸς ὑμᾶς τοῦ Θεοῦ θέλοντος ἀνήχθη ἀπὸ τῆς Ἐφέσου
verses.transliteration: alla apotaxamenos kai eipōn Palin anakampsō pros hymas tou Theou thelontos anēchthē apo tēs Ephesou
verses.literal: But as he left he said I will come back to you if God is willing And he set sail from Ephesus
verses.literalPt: mas despediu-se, dizendo: Se Deus permitir, de novo, voltarei a vós. Navegou de Éfeso,

verses.original: καὶ κατελθὼν εἰς Καισάρειαν ἀναβὰς καὶ ἀσπασάμενος τὴν ἐκκλησίαν κατέβη εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν
verses.transliteration: kai katelthōn eis Kaisareian anabas kai aspasamenos tēn ekklēsian katebē eis Antiocheian
verses.literal: When Paul had landed at Caesarea he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem Then he went down to Antioch
verses.literalPt: e, chegando a Cesareia, depois de subir a Jerusalém e saudar a igreja, desceu a Antioquia.

verses.original: Καὶ ποιήσας χρόνον τινὰ ἐξῆλθεν διερχόμενος καθεξῆς τὴν Γαλατικὴν χώραν καὶ Φρυγίαν στηρίζων πάντας τοὺς μαθητάς
verses.transliteration: Kai poiēsas chronon tina exēlthen dierchomenos kathexēs tēn Galatikēn chōran kai Phrygian stērizōn pantas tous mathētas
verses.literal: After Paul had spent some time in Antioch he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia strengthening all the disciples
verses.literalPt: Havendo estado ali algum tempo, saiu, atravessando sucessivamente a região gálata e a Frígia, fortalecendo a todos os discípulos.

verses.original: Ἰουδαῖος δέ τις Ἀπολλῶς ὀνόματι Ἀλεξανδρεὺς τῷ γένει ἀνὴρ λόγιος κατήντησεν εἰς Ἔφεσον δυνατὸς ὢν ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς
verses.transliteration: Ioudaios de tis Apollōs onomati Alexandreus tō genei anēr logios katēntēsen eis Epheson dynatos ōn en tais graphais
verses.literal: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos a native of Alexandria came to Ephesus He was an eloquent man well versed in the Scriptures
verses.literalPt: Chegou a Éfeso um judeu chamado Apolo, natural de Alexandria, homem eloquente e muito versado nas Escrituras.

verses.original: οὗτος ἦν κατηχημένος τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ ζέων τῷ πνεύματι ἐλάλει καὶ ἐδίδασκεν ἀκριβῶς τὰ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐπιστάμενος μόνον τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου
verses.transliteration: houtos ēn katēchēmenos tēn hodon tou Kyriou kai zeōn tō pneumati elalei kai edidasken akribōs ta peri tou Iēsou epistamenos monon to baptisma Iōannou
verses.literal: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus though he knew only the baptism of John
verses.literalPt: Era ele instruído no Caminho do Senhor, e, sendo fervoroso de espírito, falava, e ensinava com precisão as coisas concernentes a Jesus, apesar de conhecer somente o batismo de João;

verses.original: οὗτός τε ἤρξατο παρρησιάζεσθαι ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἀκούσαντες δὲ αὐτοῦ Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας προσελάβοντο αὐτὸν καὶ ἀκριβέστερον αὐτῷ ἐξέθεντο τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: houtos te ērxato parrēsiazesthai en tē synagōgē akousantes de autou Priskilla kai Akylas proselabonto auton kai akribesteron autō exethento tēn hodon tou Theou
verses.literal: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue When Priscilla and Aquila heard him they took him aside . . . and explained to him the way of God more accurately
verses.literalPt: e ele começou a falar ousadamente na sinagoga. Mas, quando Priscila e Áquila o ouviram, levaram-no consigo e expuseram-lhe com mais precisão o Caminho de Deus.

verses.original: Βουλομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ διελθεῖν εἰς τὴν Ἀχαΐαν προτρεψάμενοι οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἔγραψαν τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἀποδέξασθαι αὐτόν ὃς παραγενόμενος συνεβάλετο πολὺ τοῖς πεπιστευκόσιν διὰ τῆς χάριτος
verses.transliteration: Boulomenou de autou dielthein eis tēn Achaian protrepsamenoi hoi adelphoi egrapsan tois mathētais apodexasthai auton hos paragenomenos synebaleto poly tois pepisteukosin dia tēs charitos
verses.literal: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him On his arrival . . . he was a great help to those who by grace had believed
verses.literalPt: Querendo ele passar para a Acaia, os irmãos animaram-no e escreveram aos discípulos que o recebessem. Tendo ele chegado, auxiliou muito aqueles que, pela graça, haviam crido;

verses.original: εὐτόνως γὰρ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις διακατηλέγχετο δημοσίᾳ ἐπιδεικνὺς διὰ τῶν γραφῶν εἶναι τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν
verses.transliteration: eutonōs gar tois Ioudaiois diakatēlencheto dēmosia epideiknys dia tōn graphōn einai ton Christon Iēsoun
verses.literal: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ
verses.literalPt: pois com grande poder refutava publicamente os judeus, mostrando, pelas Escrituras, que Jesus era o Cristo.
